terms.grammar: adverb; closing a series: prīmum … deinde … postrēmō
evidence: Cic. Fam. 15.14.2: prīmum … deinde … tum … postrēmō
Hor. S. 1.1.106: sunt certī dēnique fīnēs
Cic. Off. 3.90: ad extrēmum … patriae salūtem antepōnet salūtī patris

phrases.english: idleness, hateful at first, is loved in the end

phrases.latin: prīmum ut tē … tantō intervallō vidērem, deinde ut tibi … possem praesēns grātulārī, … postrēmō ut amīcitia nostra … cōnfirmārētur vehementius
phrases.english: first, to see you after so long; then, to congratulate you in person; … and finally, to make our friendship stronger

denique.html: Hor. S. 1.1.106, est modus in rēbus, sunt certī dēnique fīnēs: the fifth foot, dēnique, is a dactyl. The ending is the enclitic -que.

sources: Lewis & Short: posterus (postrēmō) · Lewis & Short: denique · Lewis & Short: extremus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 315.
